section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that one should not pray except from a state of heaviness of head, and through prayer one not only nullifies this heaviness but elevates the head to the level of the skull, which is above the head, achieved through the refinement of the animal soul whose root is in the chaos that preceded rectification.
section.t: And this is: "One should not stand to pray except from a state of heaviness of head,"
and through prayer, not only does one nullify the heaviness of head,
but furthermore, it becomes "Lift up the head... of the children of Israel... according to their skulls"
(as explained in Likkutei Torah, beginning of Parshat Bamidbar),
that he elevates the head to the level of their skulls,
which is above the head.
And this is through the service of refining the animal soul,
by which he elevates the head of the G-dly soul,
for the root of the animal soul is from the aspect of the chaos that preceded rectification,
for Esav is the great firstborn,
and the abundant lights of chaos elevate the lights of rectification.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the concept of the half-shekel, where the giving from below is only a half, analogous to the two halves of a form that G-d and the Congregation of Israel complete each other, and through one's service of elevating the ten powers of the animal soul, he affects the G-dly soul above.
section.t: And this is the matter of the half-shekel,
that the giving from below is only a half,
and according to the teaching of the law
"Make for yourself two trumpets,"
two half-forms,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Congregation of Israel are two half-forms that complete each other, as it were,
and as our sages, of blessed memory, said,
"My twin, my twin."
That is,
that through his service with his ten powers, he affects above as well.
And in his service itself, the matter of the half-shekel is,
that he elevates the ten powers of the animal soul,
and through this he affects the G-dly soul,
and as above, that the abundant lights of chaos elevate the lights of rectification.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the two interpretations of "heaviness of head"—the head above and the head of the soul—explaining that just as refining the ten powers of the animal soul elevates the upper half of the G-dly soul, so too does it affect the head above, as G-d assists man in elevating his soul's powers, thereby affecting the Divine Presence.
section.t: And it can be said,
that this is also the connection
of the two interpretations of "heaviness of head,"
the head above and the head of the soul
(the G-dly soul).
For just as through the refinement of the ten powers of the animal soul,
ten gerahs,
he elevates the upper half,
the ten powers of the G-dly soul,
so too is it according to the interpretation that it refers to the head above,
for through that
(the Holy One, blessed be He, assists him, as it were)
he elevates the ten powers of his soul,
that the soul descended below,
and "authority and ability are given to every person"
etc.,
and through this he affects, as it were, also the Divine Presence, etc.
